bugs.rootCause: apps/api/src/recurring-invoices/recurring-invoices.service.ts:21-48 calcNextRunAt. The MONTHLY branch does d.setDate(1) at :33 and only THEN tests `d.getDate() > dom` at :36 — after setDate(1) the day is always 1 and dom >= 1 (DTO caps 1-28 at dto/create-recurring-invoice.dto.ts:31), so the compare is `1 > dom`, false for every legal input; the month-advance is unreachable. The function returns `dom` of the month of (from + 1 day). On the cron path `from` IS the due date (generateInvoiceFromTemplate :174 passes ri.nextRunAt, itself on dom), so the returned value equals `from`. The CAS claim at :175-178 only checks the OLD value in its WHERE, so writing an unchanged nextRunAt succeeds, and the midnight cron's `nextRunAt lte now` filter (:242) re-selects the template every night; with autoSend (:205-214) the customer is emailed a fresh invoice daily. Verified by hand trace at master 39632d27: from 2026-07-15, dom 15 -> 07-16 -> setDate(1)=07-01 -> 1>15 false -> setDate(15) -> 2026-07-15 unchanged. The only accidental escape is a non-leap February with dom 28 (the +1 day crosses the month boundary). Existing spec asserts only toBeInstanceOf(Date) at recurring-invoices.service.spec.ts:184. L-029 state sweep — every nextRunAt writer: create() :69, update() :123 (user-supplied), and the claim :174-177 (the only computed one); calcNextRunAt has exactly one caller (:174).

Return a value strictly after `from`'s calendar day. Leave the WEEKLY/BIWEEKLY code (:41-47) byte-identical and pin it with a token-less characterization test BEFORE the change. Keep local-time arithmetic (server is UTC in the Railway container — no TZ in apps/api/Dockerfile; the web's nextRunAt is a UTC-midnight calendar date rendered via fmtCalendarDate, recurring/page.tsx:157-161); tests must compare via getFullYear/getMonth/getDate so they hold in any runner TZ. bugs.fix: In generateInvoiceFromTemplate: (1) the CAS claim also stamps a PROVISIONAL `lastRunStatus: 'FAILED', lastError: 'Generation was interrupted before the invoice was created'` so a crash between claim and create can never read as success; (2) wrap invoicesService.create in try/catch — on failure write `lastRunStatus 'FAILED'`, `lastError = message.slice(0,500)`, and RESTORE `nextRunAt: ri.nextRunAt` (keep lastRunAt = attempt time), then rethrow. Make the restore a CAS too: `updateMany({ where: { id, nextRunAt: <the advanced value we wrote> }, data: {...} })` — if count === 0 a concurrent runNow already re-claimed the cycle, so fall back to writing status/lastError alone WITHOUT touching nextRunAt (this closes the race where a plain update would clobber a legitimate later claim and over-bill by one cycle). Rollback is duplicate-safe because create() has no post-commit step (see rootCause) and lets both the next midnight cron and 'Run Now' bill THIS cycle instead of the next; (3) after the existing invoice.update({ recurringInvoiceId }) link (:217-220) write `lastRunStatus 'SUCCESS', lastError: null` (optionally fold link + SUCCESS into one tenantTransaction so a mid-write blip cannot leave an invoice with a FAILED row) — this write must carry no nextRunAt (the claim stays the single schedule write). Invariant: lastError non-null iff lastRunStatus === 'FAILED'. The autoSend email failure keeps its existing log-and-leave-DRAFT behaviour and counts as SUCCESS (the invoice exists). Export the status strings as module constants. bugs.fix: ONE shared guard at the single seam every path funnels through — runSync — so the cron, all 22 hook sites, syncOrderInvoices and recomputeCommissionRange are covered without touching a caller. At the top of runSync(invoiceId, db), BEFORE the invoice findUnique at 185: `await db.$executeRaw\`SELECT id FROM "CommissionAccrual" WHERE "invoiceId" = ${invoiceId} AND "tenantId" = ${tenantId} FOR UPDATE\`` (tenantId via this.prisma.getTenantId(), already read at 53 — pass it in or re-read; raw SQL bypasses the tenant proxy so scope it by hand). This is the idiom already used at returns.service.ts:84, invoices.service.ts:4407/4624, routes.service.ts:867. Semantics: a concurrent sync blocks on this statement until the first commits; under READ COMMITTED every later statement takes a fresh snapshot, so the post-lock include sees the committed CLAWBACK, drift computes to ~0, and no second adjustment is appended. Under a Serializable caller the FOR UPDATE on a concurrently-modified row raises the same 40001 the update at 402 already would — no new failure class. The tenant tx proxy passes `$`-prefixed members through bound (prisma.service.ts:79-86) and forTenant()'s $extends client also supports $executeRaw, so `db.$executeRaw` works for every db shape runSync receives. No invoice-row lock (alternative considered: `SELECT id FROM "Invoice" … FOR UPDATE` would also serialize the create-path race, but that race is already backstopped by @@unique and locking Invoice from the hourly cron for every invoice updated in the last 25h briefly blocks live invoice writes — not worth it). Lock order stays Invoice → CommissionAccrual everywhere (hooks already hold Invoice; the cron never locks Invoice; commission-statements.service.ts only updates accruals at 208/276/309 and never writes Invoice), so no inversion. Update the class docblock (20-36) to state the lock is what makes 'append exactly one' true under concurrency.
